abstract: Motivation Despite continuing advances in sequencing and computational function prediction, large parts of gene, protein, and metabolite space remain functionally undetermined. Most function assignment is based on homology searches and annotation transfer from well-studied proteins, but this approach fails to leverage available experimental omics data generated via technologies like mass-spectrometry. Results To address this gap, we have developed the VaLPAS (Variation-Leveraged Phenomic Association Screen) framework, a Python package that provides a user-friendly platform to discover associations between expression patterns of genes, proteins, and metabolites in multi-omic datasets. VaLPAS uses various statistical and learning methods, from simple statistical methods (correlation) to a sophisticated autoencoder, to shed light on the functional dark matter of protein space using 'guilt by association' with molecules of known function. We have used VaLPAS to examine transcript, protein, and metabolite data from seven organisms across two kingdoms using two different benchmarks. We present results demonstrating the ability of VaLPAS to make high-confidence predictions of the functional associations of a subset of genes and proteins. Furthermore, we show that VaLPAS can provide insight into the functional relevance of detected but unidentified metabolites by cross-omics association, a unique feature of this approach. This ability of cross-omics association enables VaLPAS to serve as a tool for generating hypotheses of functional interaction that can be validated with targeted experiments, representing a significant step forward in elucidating dark functional matter. Availability and implementation VaLPAS is hosted on github (https://github.com/PNNL-Predictive-Phenomics/valpas/).
